key_decisions.decision: Preserves the physicians as Joseph’s servants and their distinct embalming role without labeling them priests.
Preserves the reported oath’s dug wording and Joseph’s return promise; distinguishes the nested father quotation from Joseph’s request without harmonizing it to earlier instructions.
Keeps the named threshing floor and beyond-the-Jordan wording without forcing an uncertain route; retains the separate seven-day observance.
Preserves the local observers’ Egyptian identification and the force of the heavy-mourning idiom and the place-name explanation without changing its uncertain geography.
Retains renewed fear after reconciliation and the brothers’ acknowledgment of harm rather than claiming forgiveness had removed every tension.
Presents the paternal command as the brothers’ report without declaring it either fabricated or independently verified.
Keeps offense/sin, the repeated plea, and the religious self-description; distinguishes nested quotation levels and leaves Joseph’s reason for weeping unstated.
Preserves the actual bow and offer of slavery, allowing the dream echo without inserting commentary into the verse.
Repeats intended for both agents while preserving the contrast between human harm and divine good and its stated life-preserving outcome.
Preserves the generation expression and knee image without inventing an obstetric practice or silently reducing it to generic survival.
Renders emphatic visit as effective aid, retaining ascent, the oath, and all three ancestors in source order.
Repeats the assurance exactly and preserves the oath and bones rather than replacing them with a general burial wish.
